quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If your turn signals fail, you should use ____ to show that you are turning.

options.text: Your horn
Your headlights
Hand signals
Your emergency flashers

questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to show when you are changing direction.

questions.question: When driving near children playing, you should expect them to:

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross the street.
Stop at the curb before crossing the street.
Run out in front of you without looking.
Not cross the street unless with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run out in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down and watch carefully when children are nearby. They may not understand danger and could run into the street without looking.

questions.question: ____ greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity.

options.text: High speeds
Slow speeds
Night drives
Uphill inclines

questions.explanation: High speeds greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity. The faster you drive, the harder your vehicle will hit if you crash.

questions.question: You are entering a busy freeway. What should you do to merge into traffic?

options.text: Use your side and rearview mirrors and check your blind spots.
Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of freeway traffic.
Yield to traffic already on the freeway.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Speed up on the entrance ramp to match freeway traffic speed. Yield to cars already on the freeway. Check your mirrors and blind spots before merging to make sure you have space.

questions.question: When making a right turn, your car must be:

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when you begin to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Move to the right side of the road before turning right. Do not cut across other lanes when turning.

questions.question: It is best to keep space around your vehicle:

options.text: Only in back of your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Only in front of the vehicle.
On all sides of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space on all sides of your vehicle so you can react to hazards. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left or right.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: A sudden change in weather calls for a change in driving.
You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch carefully for vehicles coming up behind you in bad weather.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Adjust your driving when weather changes suddenly. Slow down in rain and fog. Watch for vehicles behind you that may be going too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: You may drive around the gates at a railroad crossing:

options.text: When the train has passed.
Under no circumstances.
When the lights have stopped flashing.
When other drivers drive around the gates.

questions.explanation: Stop at all railroad crossings when warning signals appear. These signals include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagger, or a train's horn. Never go around a lowered gate.

questions.question: If you see this sign above your lane, you:

options.text: May not exit the freeway.
May continue through or exit the freeway from your current lane.
May stay in your lane and continue through the interchange.
Must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.
questions.explanation: An "Exit only" sign means this lane goes off the freeway. If you are under this sign, you can change lanes to continue on the freeway, or you must exit if you stay in your current lane.

questions.question: Drivers must yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Even if the pedestrian crosses the street carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
If the pedestrian uses a hand signal to ask oncoming drivers to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian crosses the street carelessly.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians in the street, even if they cross against a red light or are being careless.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement?

options.text: Stop quickly.
Pull completely off the road and get back on when it is safe.
Speed up and steer back on the road quickly.
Release the accelerator, slow down, then ease back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator, slow down, then ease back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: If your right wheels leave the pavement, don't panic. Release the accelerator and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and ease back onto the road by keeping both hands on the wheel. Turn the wheel gently to re-enter the right lane. Check for traffic before steering back onto the pavement.

questions.question: If you experience a tire blowout, what should you do?

options.text: Release the gas pedal.
Do not brake immediately.
Slow down gradually and pull off the side of the road.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: If you have a tire blowout, release the gas pedal and do not brake right away. Slow down gradually, then gently apply the brakes and pull off the side of the road.

questions.question: When should you honk your horn?

options.text: When traveling through an intersection.
When passing a bicyclist.
When you see a child about to run into the street.
When parallel parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a child about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. For example, if a child starts to run into the street in front of your vehicle, honk your horn.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk at the bicyclist to let them know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed ahead to get in front of the bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: When passing a bicyclist, slow down and give them plenty of space. Bicyclists have less protection than drivers. Passing too quickly can knock them off course.

questions.question: What about the blind spots of larger vehicles?

options.text: They are larger.
They are smaller.
They have no blind spots.
They are the same as smaller vehicles.

questions.explanation: Larger vehicles have larger blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near their rear that cannot be seen in their mirrors.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle on a two-lane road with opposite traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Return to your lane when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right side of the road immediately.
Drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to your lane when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.
questions.explanation: When passing on a two-lane road, return to the right side of the road when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you have passed.

questions.question: When must you always signal?

options.text: When changing lanes.
When pulling into or out of a parking space.
When pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when you move left or right. Signal when entering traffic from a parking space, moving to a new lane, or passing another vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do on slippery roads?

options.text: Slow down.
Drive faster.
Drive at the speed limit with caution.
Do not drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.explanation: Slow down when you see rain, snow, or sleet, as these create slippery roads. Safety may require driving slower than the posted speed limit.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Steep hill ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Low railroad crossing.
Low clearance.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that the overhead bridge or structure ahead has a low clearance. Do not pass if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign.

questions.question: What do pennant-shaped signs mean?

options.text: School zones.
No passing zones.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs indicate no passing zones. The sign will have text to confirm it is a no passing zone.

questions.question: You are driving in the right lane of a multilane highway and want to move to the left lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your turn signal.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter. Always use your turn signal when changing lanes.

questions.question: Which of these things puts distracted drivers at greater risk of a crash?

options.text: CD player
Radio
Cell phone
All of the above

questions.explanation: Using a cell phone, radio, or CD player while driving is dangerous. These devices distract you and increase your risk of a crash.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered crossing gates.
You must stop when a flagger tells you to at a railroad crossing.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing lights and gates.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop at railroad crossings when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning lights and gates. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign mean?

options.text: Warns of existing or possible hazards.
Alerts drivers to school zones.
Alerts drivers to public recreation areas.
Alerts drivers to food and gas locations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warns of existing or possible hazards.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn you of hazards ahead. These signs are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Divided highway ends.
One-way traffic ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.
Keep to the right.

questions.explanation: This sign tells you to stay to the right of the divider.
